name: Norm Winn Memorial Conservation Grant
summary: Competitive grants of up to USD 25,000 for conservation, preservation or restoration projects by 501(c)(3) organisations in Alaska, Idaho, Oregon, Montana and Eastern Washington.

geography.label: Alaska, Idaho, Oregon, Montana and Eastern Washington

reporting: Regular progress reports as set in the proposal, a final project report and a copy of any materials produced with the funding.

eligibility.rule: Request no regular operating expenses or indirect costs
Include no legislative lobbying or candidate support
Do not propose commercial ventures or feasibility studies
Do not use the grant for fund drives
Do not propose projects that could harm the environment
Have defined project start and end dates
Do not repeat established or verified studies

documents: Previous year's Profit and Loss statement
Specific detailed project budget with cash flow
Evidence of commitment from project partner organizations

deadline.text: Applications must be received by October 31, 2026.

status.quote: Applications must be received by October 31, 2026.

deadline.quote: Applications must be received by October 31, 2026.

geography.quote: Grants are limited to projects centered in Alaska, Idaho, Oregon, Montana, and Eastern Washington state.

access.quote: We do not pre-screen applications or accept letters of inquiry.

window.quote: Applications will open June 1, 2026. Applications must be received by October 31, 2026.

amount.quote: The maximum amount that may be requested is $25,000.

reporting.quote: Regular progress reports, as specified in your proposal Final project report A copy of any materials you produce with our funding

effort.quote: Applications must be received by October 31, 2026.

eligibility.quote: Regular operating expenses (e.g. overhead, ongoing or administrative salaries, or other indirect costs)
Projects that include legislative lobbying or support candidates for office
Commercial ventures or feasibility studies that might lead to commercial products or programs
Projects that could harm the environment
Projects that have no start/end dates
Projects that repeat established and/or verified studies

after_award.quote: Regular progress reports, as specified in your proposal

documents.quote: A short (4-page maximum) narrative telling us about: your organization's mission exactly what you propose to do; why it is important; how it addresses the grant's priorities; what outcomes you expect to achieve who will do the work; include either resumes or short narrative descriptions of qualifications a project schedule, including regular progress reports to the Keta Legacy Foundation

Your organization's previous year's Profit and Loss statement and current Balance Sheet (please do not include audit reports or IRS filings); and a specific detailed budget for this project, including cash flow, which shows how the grant funds, and the funds you have requested from others, will be spent Your organization's tax-exemption statement from the IRS
Evidence (e.g., a letter) of commitment from any organization you have included in your project's work scope.
